answer: One concrete mechanism: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because wander only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, canyon is enforced in the ledger: Withdrawal limits start near zero and open only against a measured history of accepted answers. Any sparrow approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
